newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN BEET TESTS SHOW LOWER SUGAR CONTENT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN BEET TESTS SHOW LOWER SUGAR CONTENT.

text.p: Romania expects to harvest 2.1 million tonnes of sugar beet this year, but recent rains have affected sugar content, a senior official said on Thursday.
"Romania's estimated 1997 beet crop is around 2.1 million tonnes," Vasile Stancu, head of Patronatul Zaharului, grouping local sugar sector employers, told Reuters by telephone.
Last year Romania harvested around 2.9 million tonnes of beet from 136,680 hectares under that crop.
A total of 147,000 hectares were planted to beets earlier this year, but earlier draught and rains in recent weeks have affected some 18,000 ha, an agriculture ministry official said.

Sugar beet tests carried out on August 10 on the remaining 128,982 ha showed sugar content at 11.2 percent, down from initial estimates 14 percent. This compares with 11.8 percent in the year-ago period.
Heavy rains and floods in recent weeks damaged vast areas of crop land and delayed wheat harvesting.

The ministry official said the adverse weather would also delay beet harvesting -- which usually starts by mid-September -- because the crop would need more time to mature. Sugar content was expected to rise to 16 percent by the time of beet harvesting in October, the official said.
Data made available to Reuters by the sugar sector employers' association showed beet root weight was 231 grams per root, as compared with 216 grams per root a year ago.
Romania's domestic sugar output is expected to be around 230,000 tonnes this year -- slightly down from 237,400 tonnes produced in 1996, a sugar industry official told Reuters.
With domestic sugar consumption hovering around 480,000 tonnes per year over the past few years, Romania would have to resort again to raw sugar imports, the official said.
